newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY AT 4-MONTH LOW, MAY TEST DOWNSIDE BEFORE RISE.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY AT 4-MONTH LOW, MAY TEST DOWNSIDE BEFORE RISE.

text.p: The Polish zloty slipped to its lowest level against the currency basket since late January on Wednesday and may test lower levels before returning to the 2.5 percent from parity resistance, dealers said.

The zloty fell to 2.24 percent from parity from Tuesday's 2.40 percent fixing as players tested the local unit's downside and foreigners sold small amounts of bills after weeks of battling central bank-enforced resistance levels.
"Market sentiment has been turning more negative for the zloty in recent days, and a further weakening cannot be ruled out," said Witold Wozniak, dealer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA.

Analysts said, however, that a Czech crown-style demise of the zloty was not likely as Poland's fundementals remained positive and foreign direct as well as portfolio investments were bound to continue to flow into Poland.

"Foreign investors are not running away from Poland and are not likely to start, so the zloty has strong potential to return to 2.5 percent from parity," said Rafal Petsch, dealer at Bank of America in London.
The zloty closed at 2.28/2.23 percent from the trading band centre, weaker than Tuesday's 2.44/2.39 percent.
It closed at 3.1450/65 to the dollar, up from 3.1510/25 on Tuesday and at 1.8650/57 to the mark, down from 1.8570/77.
Money market rates remained virtually unchanged around 22 percent on Wednesday, with overnight depos closing at 21.75/22.10 and tomorrow/next at 21.90/22.15.
